title: Section 80C Explained Simply: Where Can You Save Tax in India?
intro: Section 80C of the Income Tax Act lets you reduce your taxable income by investing in certain schemes. It is part of the old tax regime. Here is a plain-English look at the common options.

p: Under the old regime, deductions under 80C and related sections can lower taxable income up to a set limit. The new regime does not allow most of these deductions, so first compare which regime suits you.
Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and Public Provident Fund (PPF): long term and government backed.
ELSS mutual funds: market linked, with a three year lock-in.
Life insurance premiums, tuition fees for children, the principal part of a home loan, and five year tax saver fixed deposits.
Match the lock-in and risk to your goal. A retirement goal fits PPF or EPF. A long term growth goal may fit ELSS, if you can accept market ups and downs.
Do not buy a product only to save tax. A good investment should make sense even without the tax benefit.
Spread your investments across the year instead of rushing in March. It lowers the pressure and the mistakes.

faq.q: Is 80C available in the new tax regime?
faq.a: In general no, so compare both regimes with your own numbers.
